content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The placement itself is fine — `toTelephoneDisplay` as a `default` method driving a `@Mapping(... expression)` matches the established pattern in this mapper (`toCheckDigit`, `toAgeBand`, `toLocality`, `toContactPreference`, etc.), so a maintainer would find it natural. The problem is duplicated domain knowledge.

**Finding — the country dialling-code table is duplicated across the create and read paths, with no single source of truth.**

- The create endpoint already owns this table: `OwnerRestControllerV1.COUNTRY_NATIONAL_LENGTHS = Map.of("61", 9, "1", 10)` (line 447), and `validateNationalNumberLength` selects the applicable code via `.max(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length))` over the prefixes that match (lines 459–471).
- The new code re-declares the same set of codes as `TELEPHONE_COUNTRY_CODES = List.of("61", "1")` (`OwnerMapper.java:75`) and re-implements the identical longest-prefix selection (`.filter(...startsWith...).max(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length))`, lines 89–92).

The new Javadoc even concedes this — "Mirrors the create endpoint's country table" — which is the tell: two copies of the same country list that must be hand-synced. Add a country to the create endpoint's table (or change which codes are recognized) and the display formatter silently diverges, splitting a fact that this codebase otherwise keeps as a single source of truth (note the deliberate "single source of truth" framing already used for `toIdentityKey`/`hasEmail`, lines 135–147).

Suggested direction:
- Derive `TELEPHONE_COUNTRY_CODES` from the existing table rather than re-listing the codes, so the recognized set has one owner. Since `COUNTRY_NATIONAL_LENGTHS` currently lives `private static` in the controller, this means promoting the country table to a shared location (e.g. the keys exposed from wherever the table is defined) that both the create-time validation and the read-time display consult.
- Consider extracting the "longest dialling-code prefix that matches these digits" selection into one shared helper, since both sites now implement that same algorithm independently.

If lifting the table out of the controller is deemed out of scope, at minimum the two must reference a shared constant instead of each holding its own literal list.

**Finding — the country dialling-code table is duplicated across the create and read paths, with no single source of truth.**

- The create endpoint already owns this table: `OwnerRestControllerV1.COUNTRY_NATIONAL_LENGTHS = Map.of("61", 9, "1", 10)` (line 447), and `validateNationalNumberLength` selects the applicable code via `.max(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length))` over the prefixes that match (lines 459–471).
- The new code re-declares the same set of codes as `TELEPHONE_COUNTRY_CODES = List.of("61", "1")` (`OwnerMapper.java:75`) and re-implements the identical longest-prefix selection (`.filter(...startsWith...).max(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length))`, lines 89–92).

The new Javadoc even concedes this — "Mirrors the create endpoint's country table" — which is the tell: two copies of the same country list that must be hand-synced. Add a country to the create endpoint's table (or change which codes are recognized) and the display formatter silently diverges, splitting a fact that this codebase otherwise keeps as a single source of truth (note the deliberate "single source of truth" framing already used for `toIdentityKey`/`hasEmail`, lines 135–147).

Suggested direction:
- Derive `TELEPHONE_COUNTRY_CODES` from the existing table rather than re-listing the codes, so the recognized set has one owner. Since `COUNTRY_NATIONAL_LENGTHS` currently lives `private static` in the controller, this means promoting the country table to a shared location (e.g. the keys exposed from wherever the table is defined) that both the create-time validation and the read-time display consult.
- Consider extracting the "longest dialling-code prefix that matches these digits" selection into one shared helper, since both sites now implement that same algorithm independently.

If lifting the table out of the controller is deemed out of scope, at minimum the two must reference a shared constant instead of each holding its own literal list.
